newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner to reduce cable interest - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner to reduce cable interest - WSJ.

text.p: Time Warner Inc will tell its major shareholders this week that it plans to reduce its investment in the cable business as part of its efforts to cut down on its debt, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.

The newspaper said the company wants to reduce its interest in cable even if it is unable to reach an agreement with US West Communications Group, which owns 25 percent of Time Warner Entertainment. The unit includes Time Warner Cable, the country's second largest cable company with more than 11 million subscribers.
"There are things we can do to lighten up cable without US West," it quoted an unidentified senior company executive as saying.
The newspaper said Time Warner could either sell its interest in the cable systems that did not belong to its partnership with US West or spin them off completely.
